tasks.entryDescription: Pigeonhole using increasing/decreasing subsequence lengths; poset-chain/antichain formulation; permutation diagram/partition argument.
tasks.currentSketch: For each sequence position k, let f(k) be the length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at a_k. If any f(k)=n+1, the theorem follows. Otherwise f takes at most n values among n²+1 positions, so n+1 positions k₁<⋯<kₙ₊₁ share one value. Their entries must be strictly decreasing: if i<j and a_{k_i}<a_{k_j}, an increasing subsequence ending at k_i extends to k_j, contradicting equal f-values.

tasks.entryDescription: Euler product and divergence of the harmonic series; Erdős's elementary counting contradiction; compare prime-factor decompositions of integers with a hypothetical convergent reciprocal-prime sum.
tasks.routeTitle: Euler product and divergence of the harmonic series
tasks.currentSketch: For each x, the finite Euler product P_x=∏_{p≤x}(1−1/p)^{-1} expands as a sum over integers whose prime factors are at most x, so P_x≥H_x and is unbounded. If Σ_p 1/p converged, then log P_x=Σ_{p≤x}log(1+1/(p−1)) would stay bounded, since log(1+u)≤u and 1/(p−1)≤2/p for p≥2. Thus P_x would be bounded, contradiction; hence Σ_p1/p diverges. This follows the source’s Euler-product/harmonic-series argument, using the corrected harmless constant bound for the logarithm.

tasks.entryDescription: Bernstein polynomials and probabilistic binomial concentration; Stone–Weierstrass algebra/separation theorem; constructive positive-kernel approximation.
tasks.routeTitle: Bernstein polynomials and probabilistic binomial concentration
tasks.currentSketch: For continuous f on [0,1], let B_n f be its Bernstein polynomial. Uniform continuity gives |f(x)−f(a)|≤ε when |x−a|≤δ; elsewhere bound it by 2M(x−a)²/δ², where M=||f||∞. Positivity and linearity of B_n then bound |B_nf(a)−f(a)| by ε plus (2M/δ²)B_n[(x−a)²](a). The Bernstein second-moment identity gives B_n[(x−a)²](a)=a(1−a)/n≤1/(4n), uniformly in a; hence B_nf→f uniformly.

tasks.entryDescription: Extremal derivative/maximization method; normal-family/compactness method; Green-function or potential-theoretic approach in standard variants.
tasks.currentSketch: Fix a simply connected region Ω≠ℂ and z₀∈Ω and maximize |f′(z₀)| over the univalent maps Ω→D. The family is nonempty (a square-root branch of z−a, with the two branches having disjoint images, composed with an inversion) and the derivative is bounded by the Cauchy estimate. Take a maximizing sequence; the family is bounded by 1, so Montel gives a locally uniformly convergent subsequence, and Hurwitz makes the limit univalent since its derivative at z₀ is nonzero. Composing with a disc automorphism shows the maximizer sends z₀ to 0, and rotating makes f′(z₀)>0. If f(Ω)≠D, a univalent map g on f(Ω) with g(0)=0 and |g′(0)|>1 (Lecture 17) gives g∘f with larger derivative, a contradiction, so f is onto. Uniqueness follows from the Schwarz lemma.
